_note: Painted card text for words whose live card came from data/v1-payloads. build_v2.py reads this file and does not read those payloads. A layout item with "text": "vocab" skips this file. hooks.json and vocab_fixes.json still win. Edit those to change a card; do not put new words here.

fr_addition_noun.en: the bill (in a café or restaurant); also: addition, a sum
fr_addition_noun.hook: The waiter keeps ADDING each DISH ON (ah-dee-SYOHN) until THE BILL curls all the way to the floor.
fr_addition_noun.note: Ask for it at the end: l'addition, s'il vous plaît !
ex: L'addition, s'il vous plaît !
The bill, please!

falseFriend.note: In a café or restaurant, the bill. It also means addition, a sum.

fr_adresse_noun.hook: A yellow DRESS hangs on the coat stand with an ADDRESS tag pinned on it: ah-DREHS = a dress.
fr_adresse_noun.note: Spelled with one d and two s in French: une adresse. It starts with a vowel, so it's l'adresse.
ex: Quelle est ton adresse ?
What is your address?

fr_affiche_noun.hook: The POSTER on the easel shows A big orange FISH: ah-FEESH = a fish.
fr_affiche_noun.note: Feminine: UNE affiche, but l'affiche because it starts with a vowel. Coller une affiche = to put up a poster.
ex: Il y a une affiche sur le mur de la poste.
There’s a poster on the post-office wall.

fr_ajouter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe ADDS one more animal, a toy giraffe, to his little toy ZOO: ah-ZHOO-tay = a zoo + tay.
fr_ajouter_verb.note: A regular -er verb (red beret) starting with a vowel: j'ajoute. Ajouter … à … = to add … to …: ajoute deux à trois. In sums you also hear plus: deux plus trois égale cinq.
ex: Ajoute deux à trois : ça fait cinq !
Add two to three: that makes five!

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb that starts with a vowel, so je becomes j': j'ajoute.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai ajouté deux et trois. = I added two and three.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Ajoute un peu de sel ! (no s for tu in the imperative of -er verbs).

fr_allumer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe carefully LIGHTS the candles with a long taper. Allumer hides LUM, as in iLLUMinate and LUMinous: ah-lew-MAY.
fr_allumer_verb.note: Also "to switch on": allumer la lumière. The opposite is éteindre.
ex: Allume la lumière, s'il te plaît.
Turn on the light, please.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Starts with a vowel, so je becomes j': j'allume.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai allumé les bougies. = I lit the candles.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Allume la lumière ! (no s for tu in the imperative of -er verbs).

fr_appeler_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe CALLS his friend on an APPLE held to his ear and waves: ah-puh-LAY = apple + ay.
fr_appeler_verb.note: A red -er verb with one spelling change: the l doubles when the ending is silent: j'appeLLe, tu appeLLes, ils appeLLent, but nous appeLons, vous appeLez. The futur doubles too: j'appeLLerai. Je m'appelle… (= my name is…) is the same verb.
ex: J’appelle la poste pour mon colis.
I’m calling the post office about my package.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Double LL when the ending is silent (j'appelle, ils appellent); single L for nous appelons, vous appelez.

tenses.name: Futur simple
tenses.note: The LL stays in every futur form: j'appellerai, nous appellerons.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Appelle-moi ! = Call me!

fr_apprendre_verb.hook: A PRAWN in glasses helps Monsieur Verbe LEARN to read: a-PRAWN-dr!
fr_apprendre_verb.note: Built on prendre, and conjugated the same way: j'apprends, nous apprenons, ils apprennent; past participle appris. Apprendre à quelqu'un = to teach someone.
ex: J'apprends le français.
I'm learning French.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Irregular, exactly like prendre: the d drops in the plural, and ils apprennent has a double n.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai appris = I learned. Past participle: appris.

tenses.name: Subjonctif présent
tenses.note: Que j'apprenne: double n.

fr_assemblage_noun.hook: A tiny wooden go-kart is halfway through ASSEMBLY, with its loose wheel and axle beside it. Assemblage is pronounced [ah-sahn-BLAHZH].
ex: L'assemblage du meuble prend une heure.
Assembling the furniture takes an hour.

fr_asseoir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SITS DOWN in the last free café chair and admires himself in his hand mirror. Sah-SWAHR sounds like "a SWARM": he grabbed the seat before a whole SWARM of customers could!
fr_asseoir_verb.note: Gold beret = irregular, mirror = reflexive (se / s'). Asseyez-vous ! = Sit down!
ex: Asseyez-vous, s'il vous plaît.
Sit down, please.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Two correct sets of forms. The first (je m'assieds, nous nous asseyons) is the more common, especially in writing.

tenses.name: Passé composé
rows: se sont assis / se sont assises
tenses.note: Reflexive verbs take être, so the participle agrees with the subject: il s'est assis, elle s'est assise, nous nous sommes assis (or assises, all women), vous vous êtes assis(e)(s).

tenses.name: Futur simple
tenses.note: Also correct, older spelling: je m'asseyerai.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: In the positive imperative the pronoun goes after, with a hyphen: assieds-toi ! Negative: ne t'assieds pas !

fr_atelier_noun.hook: A carpenter proudly holds up the tall stool he made in his WORKSHOP, atelier [ah-tuh-LYAY]. This is a meaning picture.
ex: Je travaille dans mon atelier.
I work in my workshop.

fr_attache_noun.hook: A metal FASTENER holds a fake MUSTACHE: a TASH recalls attache [ah-TAHSH].
ex: L'attache de mon sac est cassée.
My bag's fastener is broken.

fr_attendre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe WAITS on a chair, checking his watch, next to a sun-TANNED DRAGON in sunglasses: ah-TAHNDR!
fr_attendre_verb.note: No word for 'for': j'attends le bus = I'm waiting for the bus.
ex: J'attends le bus.
I'm waiting for the bus.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -re verb: drop -re, add -s, -s, (nothing), -ons, -ez, -ent. Starts with a vowel, so j'attends.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai attendu une heure ! = I waited an hour!

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Attends ! = Wait! Attendez ici. = Wait here.

falseFriend.note: To wait (for), not to attend. To attend is assister à.

fr_baguette_noun.hook: A proud gray cat stands on top of her tower of five BAGUETTES.
fr_baguette_noun.note: English borrowed this word. French puts the stress at the end: bah-GEHT.
ex: J'achète une baguette à la boulangerie.
I buy a baguette at the bakery.

fr_balance_noun.hook: A BALL of dough and a toy LANCE sit perfectly level on the SCALES: bah-LAHNS = ball + lance.
fr_balance_noun.note: The baker weighs everything on la balance.
ex: Le boulanger pèse la farine sur la balance.
The baker weighs the flour on the scales.

falseFriend.note: Weighing scales. It also means balance, as in English.

fr_ballon_noun.hook: A beach BALL floats ON a string like a BALLOON: bah-LOHN = ball + on.
fr_ballon_noun.note: Un ballon is a big ball you kick or throw (and also a balloon). A small ball, like a tennis ball, is une balle.
ex: Les enfants jouent au ballon sur la place.
The children play ball on the square.

fr_banc_noun.hook: A pink piggy BANK sits on the BENCH: BAHN(k)! The c is silent.
fr_banc_noun.note: In a church, les bancs are the pews.
ex: Il est assis sur un banc dans le parc.
He is sitting on a bench in the park.

falseFriend.note: A bench, not a bank. A bank is la banque.

fr_beurre_noun.hook: "BRRR!" The BUTTER is so cold it shivers in a scarf and earmuffs on its icy dish. Brrr sounds like beurre.
ex: Je mets du beurre sur mon pain.
I put butter on my bread.

fr_boire_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe gulps a big glass of water like a thirsty BOAR (BWAHR). Gold beret: boire is irregular (nous buvons).
fr_boire_verb.note: Le pourboire (the tip) is "pour boire": money "for a drink".
ex: Je bois un grand verre d'eau le matin.
I drink a big glass of water in the morning.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Three stems: boi- (je bois), buv- (nous buvons), boiv- (ils boivent).

tenses.name: Subjonctif présent
tenses.note: Same stem change: que je boive, but que nous buvions.

fr_boisson_noun.hook: A big green BOA sings a SONG (bwah-SOHN) and holds up her pink lemonade DRINK.
ex: Quelle boisson voulez-vous avec votre repas ?
What drink would you like with your meal?

fr_boite_noun.hook: The cake BOX has a sail and floats away like a BOAT: BWAHT = boat.
fr_boite_noun.note: Une boîte can be a cardboard box or a can: une boîte de gâteaux. The î has a circumflex.
ex: Mets les gâteaux dans la boîte.
Put the cakes in the box.

fr_bol_noun.hook: A kitten curls up asleep in a big breakfast BOWL. Bol sounds like BOWL.
fr_bol_noun.note: French breakfast: hot chocolate or coffee in a bowl.
ex: Je bois mon chocolat dans un bol.
I drink my hot chocolate from a bowl.

fr_bougie_noun.hook: A cheerful little CANDLE does the BOOGIE (boo-ZHEE) on its brass holder.
fr_bougie_noun.note: Une bougie is any everyday candle. The tall candles in a church are often called des cierges.
ex: Il souffle les bougies de son gâteau.
He blows out the candles on his cake.

fr_boulanger_noun.hook: The jolly BAKER juggles three warm croissants. He works in la boulangerie (the bakery): drop the shop's ending -ie and you get the baker.
fr_boulanger_noun.note: This hook works through spelling, not sound.
ex: Le boulanger se lève très tôt.
The baker gets up very early.

fr_boule_noun.hook: A shiny round BALL sits in a blue BOWL: BOOL = bowl.
fr_boule_noun.note: La boule is a solid round shape (a sphere, a pétanque ball, a scoop of ice cream). A ball you play soccer with is un ballon.
ex: La boule roule sous la table.
The ball rolls under the table.

fr_boulier_noun.hook: Its colored beads are little BOULES (balls) on wires: boo-LYAY = boules on wires. Tap it to hear the numbers!
fr_boulier_noun.note: Not in the course word list. Built on la boule: un boulier is a frame of boules for counting.
ex: Je compte jusqu'à vingt avec le boulier.
I count to twenty with the abacus.

notes.d: 70 = soixante-dix (60 + 10). Keep going with the teens: 71 soixante et onze, 75 soixante-quinze, 79 soixante-dix-neuf.
80 = quatre-vingts (4 × 20). The s goes when another number follows: 81 = quatre-vingt-un (and no et).
21, 31, 41, 51 and 61 use et: vingt et un, trente et un … and 71 is soixante et onze. All the others use a hyphen: vingt-deux, trente-cinq. 81 and 91 have no et.
No un in front: cent (100), mille (1000). Mille never takes an s: deux mille. In Belgium and Switzerland you also hear septante (70) and nonante (90).

fr_bricolage_noun.hook: A craftswoman assembles a BRICK COLLAGE: a homemade DIY project, bricolage [bree-koh-LAHZH].
ex: Mon père adore le bricolage.
My father loves DIY.

fr_buche_noun.hook: A leafy BUSH grows out of the LOG: BEWSH = bush.
fr_buche_noun.note: Wood ovens burn des bûches. At Christmas, la bûche de Noël is a log-shaped cake.
ex: Mets une bûche dans le four.
Put a log in the oven.

fr_bureau_noun.hook: A gray BURRO (donkey) in glasses works at his DESK in the OFFICE: bew-ROH.
fr_bureau_noun.note: Both the desk and the room: le bureau. Plural with -x: les bureaux.
ex: Mon père travaille dans un bureau.
My father works in an office.

falseFriend.note: A desk or an office, not a chest of drawers (une commode).

fr_cadeau_noun.hook: Open the PRESENT: it is full of soft modeling DOUGH: kah-DOH = (play-)dough.
fr_cadeau_noun.note: Plural with x: des cadeaux. Faire un cadeau à quelqu’un = to give someone a present.
ex: C’est un cadeau pour toi !
It’s a present for you!

fr_cafe_noun.hook: A sleepy owl hugs a cup of black COFFEE to wake up: CAFÉ, the same word as the place where you drink it.
fr_cafe_noun.note: Un café on its own is a small black coffee; with milk it is un café au lait or un crème.
ex: Je prends un café avec du lait.
I'm having a coffee with milk.

fr_cahier_noun.hook: The EXERCISE BOOK is folded into a little blue KAYAK, paddle and all: kah-YAY = kayak!
fr_cahier_noun.note: The h is silent: ka-YAY. Un cahier de brouillon = a rough-work book.
ex: Ouvrez vos cahiers.
Open your exercise books.

fr_caisse_noun.en: till, cash register; also: crate, box
fr_caisse_noun.hook: The shiny brass till is the shop's money CASE: you put the CASH in the CASE. Case sounds like caisse (KEHS).
fr_caisse_noun.note: In shops, "à la caisse" means "at the checkout".
ex: Payez à la caisse, s'il vous plaît.
Please pay at the till.

fr_carre_noun.hook: The blue SQUARE drives its little red CAR and shouts “hoo-RAY!”: kah-RAY = car + (hoo)ray.
fr_carre_noun.note: Also an adjective: une table carrée = a square table. Un mètre carré = a square meter.
ex: Un carré a quatre côtés égaux.
A square has four equal sides.

fr_carte_identite_noun.hook: Your ID CARD zooms up to the counter in a little red go-KART: KAHRT d'identité.
fr_carte_identite_noun.note: Carte is feminine, so the whole thing is: la carte d'identité. Une pièce d'identité = any proof of identity.
ex: Montrez votre carte d'identité, s'il vous plaît.
Show your identity card, please.

fr_carte_noun.en: menu (in a café); also: card, map
fr_carte_noun.hook: A little go-KART zooms in carrying the café MENU. Kart sounds like carte.
fr_carte_noun.note: Le menu often means a fixed-price set meal.
ex: La carte, s'il vous plaît.
The menu, please.

falseFriend.note: In a café, the menu. It also means a card or a map.

fr_carton_noun.hook: The CARDBOARD BOX rolls like a CAR and carries a heavy weight, a whole TON: kahr-TOHN = car + ton.
fr_carton_noun.note: Une boîte en carton = a cardboard box.
ex: Mets les livres dans le carton.
Put the books in the cardboard box.

falseFriend.note: Cardboard or a cardboard box, not a carton of milk. That is une brique de lait.

fr_casquette_noun.hook: A smiling CASSETTE tape wears the mail carrier’s blue CAP: kahs-KEHT = cassette.
fr_casquette_noun.note: La casquette has a peak (visor); le chapeau is a hat in general. La casquette du facteur = the mail carrier’s cap.
ex: Le facteur porte une casquette bleue.
The mailman wears a blue cap.

fr_cercle_noun.hook: The orange hoop is a perfect CIRCLE: SEHRKL = circle, said the French way.
fr_cercle_noun.note: Masculine: UN cercle. Dessiner un cercle avec un compas = to draw a circle with a compass. En cercle = in a circle.
ex: Les enfants sont assis en cercle.
The children are sitting in a circle.

fr_chaise_noun.hook: Grandma has sunk so deep into the cushion of her CHAIR that everyone laughs: "SHE'S stuck!" She's sounds like chaise.
ex: Prends une chaise et assieds-toi.
Take a chair and sit down.

fr_chanter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SINGS softly from his songbook: a gentle CHANT, "chant-AY".
fr_chanter_verb.note: Une chanson = a song; le chant = singing; la chorale = the choir.
ex: Les enfants chantent une chanson.
The children are singing a song.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb: je chante, tu chantes and il chante all sound the same (SHAHNT).

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Chante ! (no s for tu in the imperative of -er verbs).

fr_chapeau_noun.hook: A dapper straw HAT with a monocle and mustache, a real CHAP, says “OH!”: shah-POH = chap + oh.
fr_chapeau_noun.note: Plural with -x: des chapeaux. Chapeau ! on its own means “well done!”.
ex: Il fait chaud, mets ton chapeau.
It’s hot, put your hat on.

fr_chiffre_noun.hook: The wooden DIGIT 7 wears a CHEF's hat: SHEEFR = chef + r.
fr_chiffre_noun.note: Un chiffre is one digit (0 to 9): 25 is un nombre with deux chiffres. A number on a ticket or phone is un numéro.
ex: Le nombre 25 a deux chiffres.
The number 25 has two digits.

fr_chocolat_noun.hook: The HOT CHOCOLATE gets a SHOCK (zap!) and sings “LA!”: shoh-koh-LAH = shock-o-la.
fr_chocolat_noun.note: Un chocolat chaud = a hot chocolate. The final t is silent.
ex: Un chocolat chaud, s’il vous plaît.
A hot chocolate, please.

fr_choisir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe taps his chin and CHOOSES a treat on the counter. CHOisir starts like CHOose: cho-, choose.
fr_choisir_verb.note: This hook works through spelling, not sound: say shwah-ZEER.
ex: Choisis un gâteau !
Choose a cake!

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Regular -ir verbs add -iss- in the plural: nous choisissons.

fr_ciseau_noun.hook: A CHISEL cuts a spiral into a limestone block. Ciseau is pronounced [see-ZOH]; this is a meaning picture.
ex: Le sculpteur travaille le bois au ciseau.
The sculptor works the wood with a chisel.
fr_ciseau_noun.note: Un ciseau is a chisel; les ciseaux usually means scissors.

fr_ciseaux_noun.hook: The SCISSORS play on a little wooden SEESAW: see-ZOH!
fr_ciseaux_noun.note: Always plural, like in English, and masculine: les ciseaux, des ciseaux. One pair is une paire de ciseaux.
ex: Fais attention avec les ciseaux.
Be careful with the scissors.

fr_cle_noun.hook: A slab of CLAY holds a deep KEY impression, with the silver key at its foot. CLAY recalls clé [KLAY].
ex: J'ai perdu ma clé.
I've lost my key.

fr_clou_noun.hook: A magnifying glass examines a fingerprint on a NAIL as a CLUE: clou [KLOO].
ex: Il plante un clou dans le mur.
He hammers a nail into the wall.

fr_colis_noun.hook: A fluffy COLLIE dog proudly carries the PARCEL in its mouth: koh-LEE = collie.
fr_colis_noun.note: Same in the plural: un colis, des colis (the s is silent). Envoyer un colis = to send a package.
ex: Le colis arrive demain.
The package arrives tomorrow.

fr_colle_noun.hook: A COLLIE puppy has its paw stuck to the GLUE bottle: KOL = collie.
fr_colle_noun.note: Coller = to stick. Un bâton de colle = a glue stick.
ex: Passe-moi la colle, s'il te plaît.
Pass me the glue, please.

fr_commander_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe raises a finger like a COMMANDER and ORDERS from the menu: "koh-mahn-DAY!"
fr_commander_verb.note: Je voudrais commander = I would like to order.
ex: Nous commandons une pizza.
We're ordering a pizza.

tenses.name: Conditionnel présent
tenses.note: Polite ordering: je voudrais… or nous aimerions commander.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: No -s on the tu form of -er verbs: commande !

falseFriend.note: To order (food, goods). It can mean to command, but in a café it means to order.

fr_compas_noun.hook: The COMPASS stands on its needle and draws a circle: kohn-PAH = compass, with a silent s.
fr_compas_noun.note: Not in the course word list. Same in the plural: des compas.
ex: Je trace un cercle avec mon compas.
I draw a circle with my compasses.

falseFriend.note: Compasses for drawing circles, not a compass for finding north. That is une boussole.

fr_compter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe COUNTS the coins on his fingers: one, two, three! Compter is COUNT with a French ending, and the p stays quiet.
fr_compter_verb.note: Spelling tip: compter keeps a silent p (like English "account").
ex: L'enfant compte jusqu'à dix.
The child counts to ten.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: The p is silent in every form: je compte = zhuh KOHNT.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: No -s on the tu form of -er verbs: compte !

fr_courrier_noun.hook: A bundle of letters in running shoes sprints off like a COURIER: koo-RYAY = courier.
fr_courrier_noun.note: Le courrier = all the letters together (the mail), usually singular. Le courrier est arrivé ? = Has the post come?
ex: Le facteur apporte le courrier le matin.
The mailman brings the mail in the morning.

falseFriend.note: The mail (letters and post), not a courier. A courier is un coursier.

fr_couteau_noun.hook: A dove COOs on the KNIFE, perched on its TOE: koo-TOH = coo + toe.
fr_couteau_noun.note: Plural with -x: des couteaux. A fork is une fourchette, a spoon une cuillère.
ex: Il manque un couteau sur la table.
There’s a knife missing from the table.

fr_craie_noun.hook: A red CRAYfish holds up a big stick of CHALK: KREH = cray(fish).
fr_craie_noun.note: Un morceau de craie = a piece of chalk. Silent -ie at the end: just KREH.
ex: Le tableau est plein de craie.
The board is covered in chalk.

fr_crayon_noun.hook: False friend! This PENCIL is in disguise, wearing a rainbow CRAYON wrapper. Un crayon is a pencil.
fr_crayon_noun.note: Un crayon de couleur = a coloring pencil.
ex: Je dessine avec un crayon.
I'm drawing with a pencil.

falseFriend.note: A pencil, not a crayon. A wax crayon is un crayon de cire or une craie grasse.

fr_crepe_noun_f.hook: The thin PANCAKE wears a big bow of pink CREPE paper: KREHP = crepe.
fr_crepe_noun_f.note: The pancake is LA crêpe (feminine). Le crêpe (masculine) is a crinkly fabric. Une crêpe au sucre = a sugar crêpe.
ex: Je voudrais une crêpe au chocolat.
I would like a chocolate crêpe.

fr_croissant_noun.hook: A croissant curved just like the CRESCENT moon above it. The French word croissant also means crescent (and growing).
fr_croissant_noun.note: Not in the project word list as a noun; card written for this room. Say krwah-SAHN, no "t" at the end.
ex: Je mange un croissant au petit déjeuner.
I eat a croissant for breakfast.

fr_cube_noun.hook: A cool ICE CUBE smiles: KEWB = cube, with the French u (lips round, say ee).
fr_cube_noun.note: An ice cube is un glaçon; un cube is the shape, or a toy building block. Les cubes = building blocks.
ex: Le dé est un petit cube.
A die is a little cube.

fr_cuire_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe, in a CHOIR-boy collar, sings "O!" while he COOKS a pancake: KWEER = choir.
fr_cuire_verb.note: Irregular: je cuis, nous cuisons, ils cuisent; past participle cuit. Faire cuire = to cook something: je fais cuire le pain.
ex: Le pain cuit dans le four.
The bread is baking in the oven.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Irregular: an -s- appears in the plural (nous cuisons, ils cuisent), like conduire and construire.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: Le pain est cuit ! = The bread is baked (done)!

tenses.name: Futur simple
tenses.note: The future keeps the whole infinitive minus the final e: je cuirai.

fr_date_noun.hook: A DART lands in one square of the calendar: that is the DATE: DAHT = dart.
fr_date_noun.note: Quelle est la date aujourd'hui ? = What is the date today?
ex: Écris la date en haut de la lettre.
Write the date at the top of the letter.

falseFriend.note: Only a calendar date. A date with someone is un rendez-vous.

fr_de_noun.hook: The DIE in sunglasses holds up the sun: what a lovely DAY! DAY = dé.
fr_de_noun.note: Un dé, des dés = one die, two dice. Lance le dé ! = Roll the die! Un dé à coudre = a thimble.
ex: Lance le dé : c'est un six !
Roll the die: it's a six!

fr_demander_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe raises his hand with a question mark. He does not DEMAND, he ASKS politely: demander = to ask.
fr_demander_verb.note: Demander quelque chose = to ask for something: je demande la carte. A regular -er verb.
ex: Je demande l’addition, s’il vous plaît.
I’m asking for the bill, please.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent. Only nous and vous sound different.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai demandé la carte. = I asked for the menu.

falseFriend.note: To ask, not to demand. To demand is exiger.

fr_dire_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe wears DEER antlers and SAYS something kind, with a heart in his speech bubble: DEER = dire.
fr_dire_verb.note: Irregular: je dis, nous disons, but vous DITES (like vous faites). Past participle dit. Dire quelque chose à quelqu'un = to tell someone something.
ex: Dis « merci » au serveur.
Say “thank you” to the waiter.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Irregular: vous DITES (not disez), like vous faites and vous êtes.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: Qu'est-ce que tu as dit ? = What did you say?

fr_diviser_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe the DIVER, in goggles and flippers, DIVIDES a pizza into equal slices: dee-vee-ZAY = divide.
fr_diviser_verb.note: A regular -er verb (red beret). Diviser par = to divide by: dix divisé par deux égale cinq. Diviser en = to divide into: en huit parts.
ex: On divise la pizza en huit parts.
We divide the pizza into eight slices.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb: je divise, tu divises and il divise all sound the same (dee-VEEZ). The s between vowels sounds like z.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai divisé la pizza en huit. = I divided the pizza into eight.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Divise par deux ! = Divide by two!

fr_drapeau_noun.hook: The FLAG is DRAPED over its little stand. DRAPE... OH! drah-POH.
fr_drapeau_noun.note: Words ending in -eau are usually masculine and take -x in the plural: les drapeaux.
ex: Le drapeau français est bleu, blanc, rouge.
The French flag is blue, white and red.

fr_eau_noun.hook: The WATER pitcher gasps "OH!" as the water splashes out: l’eau = OH.
fr_eau_noun.note: Feminine, but you hear only l’ before it: de l’eau = some water. Three letters, one sound: OH.
ex: Il faut de l’eau pour faire la pâte.
You need water to make the dough.

fr_echelle_noun.hook: A SHELL rests on top of a wooden LADDER: a shell recalls échelle [ay-SHEHL].
ex: Il monte sur l'échelle.
He climbs up the ladder.

fr_eclair_noun.en: éclair (cream pastry); also: flash of lightning
fr_eclair_noun.hook: A greedy mouse lounges on a giant chocolate ÉCLAIR, ready to gobble it in a flash: in French, éclair also means a FLASH OF LIGHTNING.
fr_eclair_noun.note: Same word in English; French says ay-KLEHR.
ex: Je voudrais un éclair au chocolat, s'il vous plaît.
I'd like a chocolate éclair, please.

fr_ecouter_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe cups his ear to LISTEN to a white dove: COO! ay-COO-tay.
fr_ecouter_verb.note: No word for 'to': j'écoute la maîtresse = I'm listening to the teacher. Écoutez ! = Listen!
ex: Écoutez bien la maîtresse.
Listen carefully to the teacher.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb. It starts with a vowel, so j'écoute.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Écoutez ! = Listen! (no s for tu: écoute !)

fr_ecrire_verb.hook: Like a town CRIER, Monsieur Verbe calls out each word as he WRITES it on a long scroll: ay-KREER = a crier.
fr_ecrire_verb.note: Irregular: j'écris, but nous écrivons. Past participle: écrit (j'ai écrit).
ex: J'écris une carte postale.
I'm writing a postcard.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Irregular: a v appears in the plural (nous écrivons, vous écrivez, ils écrivent). Starts with a vowel, so j'écris.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai écrit une lettre. = I wrote a letter.

tenses.name: Futur simple
tenses.note: Stem écrir-: j'écrirai.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Écris-moi ! = Write to me!

fr_emballer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe in a pink tutu does BALLET on tiptoe while he WRAPS a package: ahn-bah-LAY = (en) ballet.
fr_emballer_verb.note: A regular -er verb (red beret): j’emballe, nous emballons. Emballer un cadeau = to wrap a present. Le papier d’emballage = wrapping paper.
ex: Nous emballons le cadeau avec du papier bleu.
We’re wrapping the present in blue paper.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb that starts with a vowel, so je becomes j': j'emballe.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai emballé le cadeau. = I wrapped the present.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Emballe le colis ! (no s for tu in the imperative of -er verbs).

fr_enveloppe_noun.hook: A LOP-eared bunny licks the ENVELOPE shut: ahn-vuh-LOP!
fr_enveloppe_noun.note: Two p in French: enveloppe. Feminine: une enveloppe.
ex: Mets la lettre dans l'enveloppe.
Put the letter in the envelope.

fr_envoyer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe is the village ENVOY: he SENDS a paper-plane letter flying and shouts “YAY!”: ahn-vwah-YAY = envoy + yay.
fr_envoyer_verb.note: Why a GOLD beret? Envoyer has -er endings, but its futur and conditionnel are irregular: j'ENVERRAI, j'ENVERRAIS (not envoyerai), so you cannot build every tense from the infinitive. Also y becomes i before a silent e: j'envoie, ils envoient, but nous envoyons. Envoyer une lettre à quelqu'un = to send someone a letter.
ex: J’envoie une carte à ma grand-mère.
I’m sending a card to my grandmother.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: -er endings, but y becomes i before a silent ending: j'envoie, ils envoient; nous envoyons, vous envoyez keep the y.

tenses.name: Futur simple
tenses.note: Irregular stem ENVERR- (like voir: je verrai): j'enverrai, not envoyerai. That is why Monsieur Verbe wears a gold beret here.

tenses.name: Conditionnel présent
tenses.note: Same irregular stem as the futur: j'enverrais.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Envoie la lettre ! (no s for tu, as with other -er verbs).

fr_etiquette_noun.hook: A blue TEA KETTLE wears a brown LABEL on its handle: ay-tee-KEHT = (a) tea-kett(le).
ex: Colle l’étiquette sur le colis.
Stick the label on the package.

falseFriend.note: A label or tag. It also means etiquette (good manners), as in English.

fr_etoile_noun.hook: The STAR has just had its bath and is wrapped in A TOWEL: ay-TWAHL = a towel.
fr_etoile_noun.note: Feminine: UNE étoile, but l'étoile because it starts with a vowel. Une étoile de mer = a starfish.
ex: Dessine une étoile à cinq branches.
Draw a five-pointed star.

fr_farine_noun.hook: A big sack of FLOUR with a wooden scoop. Think of FARINA, the English name for a fine wheat-flour cereal: fah-REEN.
ex: Il faut de la farine pour faire un gâteau.
You need flour to make a cake.

fr_feuille_noun.hook: This SHEET of writing paper is shaped like a LEAF, because French uses one word for both: la feuille.
fr_feuille_noun.note: Une feuille de papier = a sheet of paper; une feuille d’arbre = a leaf. The ending -euille sounds like “uhy”.
ex: Donne-moi une feuille, s’il te plaît.
Give me a sheet of paper, please.

fr_ficelle_noun.hook: A shop-mouse holds a payment FEE beside the TWINE it is selling. FEE–SELL loosely cues ficelle [fee-SEHL].
ex: Il attache le paquet avec une ficelle.
He ties the package with string.

fr_file_noun.hook: Three EELS wait patiently in a QUEUE at the town hall, the first one holding its ticket. Eel... FEEL! La file is the line.
fr_file_noun.note: La file d'attente = the waiting line. Faire la queue (or faire la file) = to line up.
ex: Il y a une longue file d'attente.
There's a long line.

falseFriend.note: A line of people, not a file. A computer file is un fichier; a paper file is un dossier.

fr_finir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe bursts through the ribbon: the FINISH is NEAR! fee-NEER.
fr_finir_verb.note: The model -ir verb: nous finissons, ils finissent. J'ai fini ! = I'm done!
ex: La classe finit à quatre heures.
Class finishes at four o'clock.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: The model regular -ir verb: -is, -is, -it, then -iss- in the plural (nous finissons).

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai fini ! = I've finished!

fr_fleche_noun.hook: The red ARROW zooms past in a FLASH: FLEHSH = flash.
fr_fleche_noun.note: The arrow you shoot and the arrow sign (→) are both une flèche. Suis la flèche ! = Follow the arrow!
ex: La flèche montre la bonne réponse.
The arrow points to the right answer.

fr_fleur_noun.hook: A FLURRY (FLUHR) of petals swirls round a happy bumblebee next to a big vase of FLOWERS.
fr_fleur_noun.note: The eu sounds like the u in "fur", with rounded lips.
ex: Elle m'a offert des fleurs.
She gave me some flowers.

fr_four_noun.hook: The OVEN wears a cozy FUR stole: FOOR = fur.
fr_four_noun.note: Said FOOR. Au four = in the oven, baked.
ex: Le four est très chaud.
The oven is very hot.

falseFriend.note: An oven. It is spelled like English 'four', but the number four is quatre.

fr_gant_noun.hook: The oven GLOVE is a knight’s GAUNTlet, with metal plates: GAHN = gaunt(let).
fr_gant_noun.note: The t is silent: GAHN. Un gant de cuisine = an oven glove.
ex: Prends le gant, le plateau est chaud !
Take the oven glove, the tray is hot!

fr_garage_noun.hook: A red car is parked inside a miniature GARAGE. The French word sounds gah-RAHZH, with a soft zh ending.
ex: La voiture est au garage.
The car is in the garage.

fr_gateau_noun.hook: A tall strawberry layer CAKE on its stand. English uses "gâteau" for a fancy cream cake too; say it the French way, gah-TOH.
fr_gateau_noun.note: Plural adds an x: les gâteaux.
ex: Maman fait un gâteau au chocolat.
Mom is making a chocolate cake.

fr_glace_noun.hook: Three scoops of ICE CREAM piled high in a tall GLASS (GLAHS).
ex: Les enfants mangent une glace à la fraise.
The children are eating a strawberry ice cream.

falseFriend.note: Ice cream, ice or a mirror, but never a drinking glass. A glass is un verre.

fr_globe_noun.hook: A wobbly GLOB of blue Jell-O sits on top of the GLOBE: GLOB!
fr_globe_noun.note: Same word as in English, but said with a short o: GLOB. Le globe terrestre = the globe of the Earth.
ex: Montre-moi la France sur le globe.
Show me France on the globe.

fr_gomme_noun.hook: This pink ERASER looks just like a stick of GUM in its silver wrapper: GOM = gum.
ex: Tu as une gomme ?
Do you have an eraser?

falseFriend.note: An eraser (an eraser), not chewing gum. Gum is un chewing-gum.

fr_horloge_noun.en: clock (a big one, e.g. on a tower)
fr_horloge_noun.hook: Someone has leaned an OAR on the big tower CLOCK, which is as big as a LODGE: OAR-LODGE, or-LOZH.
fr_horloge_noun.note: Une horloge is a big clock; an alarm clock is un réveil and a watch is une montre. The h is silent.
ex: L'horloge de la gare indique midi.
The station clock shows noon.

fr_jus_noun.hook: A baby giraffe from the ZOO (ZHEW) sips a big glass of ORANGE JUICE through a curly straw.
fr_jus_noun.note: Le jus = juice; the s is silent. Lips round like "ew" for the u.
ex: Je bois un jus d'orange au petit déjeuner.
I drink an orange juice at breakfast.

fr_lecon_noun.hook: A little SUN in glasses gives today's LESSON at its easel: luh-SOHN, the LESSON from the SUN.
fr_lecon_noun.note: The cédille under the c (ç) makes it a soft s sound: le-SON, not le-KON.
ex: Apprends ta leçon pour demain.
Learn your lesson for tomorrow.

fr_lettre_noun.hook: A LETTER sealed with a red heart: LET it be TRUE! LEHTR.
fr_lettre_noun.note: Both a letter you mail and a letter of the alphabet.
ex: J'écris une lettre à mon ami.
I'm writing a letter to my friend.

fr_ligne_noun.hook: The purple LINE LEANS on its tightrope and keeps its balance: LEENY = lean-y.
fr_ligne_noun.note: The gn sounds like ny in canyon. Une ligne droite = a straight line. À la ligne ! = new line!
ex: Trace une ligne droite avec la règle.
Draw a straight line with the ruler.

fr_lunette_noun.hook: These GLASSES have two crescent MOONS for lenses: la lune = the moon, so lunettes = “little moons”.
fr_lunette_noun.note: Always plural for glasses: des lunettes (feminine). Des lunettes de soleil = sunglasses. Une lunette (singular) is a telescope.
ex: Mets tes lunettes de soleil !
Put on your sunglasses!

fr_maire_noun.hook: The MAYOR is a MARE wearing the red, white and blue sash, ready to cut the ribbon with golden scissors: MEHR = mare.
fr_maire_noun.note: Traditionally masculine (le maire, even for a woman: Madame le maire); la maire is now common too. Don't mix it up with la mer (the sea) or la mère (the mother): they sound the same!
ex: Le maire inaugure la nouvelle école.
The mayor opens the new school.

fr_maitresse_noun.hook: The teacher reads a story standing on a big blue story-time MATTRESS: meh-TRESS!
fr_maitresse_noun.note: Young students call their teacher la maîtresse (a woman) or le maître (a man). From high school on, it's le or la professeur, or simply le or la prof.
ex: La maîtresse lit une histoire.
The teacher is reading a story.

falseFriend.note: At school, the (woman) teacher of young children. In other contexts it can mean a mistress, so context matters.

fr_manivelle_noun.hook: A toy MAN on one KNEE turns the hand CRANK of a tiny WELL. MAN–KNEE–WELL loosely cues manivelle [mah-nee-VEHL].
ex: Il tourne la manivelle pour ouvrir le store.
He turns the crank to open the blind.

fr_marteau_noun.hook: A red toy MARtian holds a HAMMER above its boot TOE. MAR–TOE loosely cues marteau [mahr-TOH].
ex: Passe-moi le marteau.
Pass me the hammer.

fr_melanger_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe MIXES the batter inside half a water-MELON: MAY-lahn = melon.
fr_melanger_verb.note: A -ger verb: keep the e before a and o so the g stays soft: nous mélangeons, je mélangeais.
ex: Mélange la farine et l’eau.
Mix the flour and the water.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A -ger verb: nous mélangEons keeps an e so the g stays soft (zh) before o.

tenses.name: Imparfait
tenses.note: The e stays before a: je mélangeais, but nous mélangions, vous mélangiez.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Mélange ! (no s for tu in the imperative of -er verbs).

fr_menu_noun.hook: A kitten going “MEW” reads the MENU: muh-NEW = mew.
ex: Je prends le menu du jour.
I’ll have the set menu of the day.

falseFriend.note: Usually a fixed-price set meal (le menu du jour), not the list of all the dishes. That list is la carte.

fr_mesurer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe MEASURES the tall sunflower right up to its sunny petals: muh-zew-RAY = measure + ray (of sunshine).
fr_mesurer_verb.note: A regular -er verb (red beret). It also gives your height: je mesure un mètre trente = I'm 1.30 m tall. Combien tu mesures ? = How tall are you?
ex: Je mesure la ligne avec ma règle.
I'm measuring the line with my ruler.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb: je mesure, tu mesures, il mesure all sound the same (muh-ZEWR). Je mesure un mètre vingt = I'm 1.20 m tall.

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: Nous avons mesuré la table. = We measured the table.

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Mesure la ligne avec ta règle !

fr_moitie_noun.hook: HALF an orange wears a smart bow tie and says: “MY TIE, yay!”: mwah-TYAY.
fr_moitie_noun.note: La moitié de = half of: la moitié de la classe. In sums, a half is un demi (½). Moitié-moitié = half and half.
ex: Je te donne la moitié de mon orange.
I'll give you half of my orange.

fr_monnaie_noun.hook: A blue saucer heaped with shiny coins: small MONEY, the change. Moh-NEH sounds like MONEY.
ex: Vous avez de la monnaie sur vingt euros ?
Do you have change for twenty euros?

falseFriend.note: Change or currency, not money in general. Money is l'argent.

fr_moule_noun_m.hook: A MULE wears the cake TIN as a hat: MOOL = mule.
fr_moule_noun_m.note: Watch out: la moule (feminine) is a mussel. The baking pan is LE moule.
ex: Verse la pâte dans le moule.
Pour the batter into the pan.

fr_nappe_noun.hook: The checked TABLECLOTH curls up in a nightcap and takes a NAP: NAHP = nap.
fr_nappe_noun.note: Une nappe à carreaux = a checked tablecloth. Mettre la nappe = to lay the tablecloth.
ex: La nappe est rouge et blanche.
The tablecloth is red and white.

fr_nom_noun.hook: A cheerful GNOME points to the blank NAME badge on his chest: what is your NAME, gnome?
fr_nom_noun.note: Le nom is usually the surname; the first name is le prénom. In grammar, un nom is a noun.
ex: Quel est ton nom ?
What is your name?

fr_numero_noun.hook: Take a NUMBER from the red ticket machine and wait in a NEW ROW: new-may-ROH = new … row.
fr_numero_noun.note: Le numéro is a number that labels something: ton numéro de téléphone. A number in math is un nombre.
ex: J’ai le numéro sept.
I’ve got number seven.

fr_oeuf_noun.plural: les œufs (said "lay ZUH": the f goes silent)
fr_oeuf_noun.hook: "OOF!" The EGG strains to lift a heavy barbell. Oof sounds like œuf.
ex: Je mange un œuf au petit déjeuner.
I eat an egg for breakfast.

fr_outil_noun.hook: A wrench, a TOOL, grips a cup of TEA. TEA cues only the end of outil [oo-TEE].
ex: Mon père range ses outils dans le garage.
My father keeps his tools in the garage.

fr_paille_noun.hook: A striped drinking STRAW is stuck right into a PIE: PAHY = pie.
fr_paille_noun.note: La paille is also the straw farmers use. Un chapeau de paille = a straw hat.
ex: Je peux avoir une paille ?
Can I have a straw?

fr_pain_noun.hook: Sounds like PAN: a round loaf of BREAD has puffed right up out of a frying PAN.
ex: Je mange du pain avec du beurre.
I eat bread with butter.

falseFriend.note: Bread, not pain. Pain (hurt) is la douleur.

fr_panier_noun.hook: A wicker bike PANNIER full of rolls and baguettes. A pannier is a basket bag: pannier, panier (pah-NYAY).
ex: Elle met les pommes dans le panier.
She puts the apples in the basket.

fr_paquet_noun.hook: The little PACKET gives an “OK” sign: it is packed and ready: pah-KEH = pack + OK.
fr_paquet_noun.note: The t is silent: pah-KEH. Un paquet de biscuits = a pack of cookies.
ex: Le paquet est prêt pour la poste.
The package is ready for the post.

fr_passeport_noun.hook: A duck in a yellow raincoat shows his PASSPORT while the rain POURS down: PASS, POUR! pahs-POR.
fr_passeport_noun.note: Spelled with an e in the middle: passeport. The final t is silent.
ex: N'oublie pas ton passeport !
Don't forget your passport!

fr_pate_noun.hook: A happy ball of DOUGH PATS its round tummy on a floury board. PAT sounds like pâte.
fr_pate_noun.note: Not pâté (pah-TAY, a meat spread). Les pâtes (plural) means pasta.
ex: Je prépare la pâte à crêpes.
I'm making the pancake batter.

fr_payer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe PAYS with a big gold coin and punches the air: PAY... YAY!
ex: Je paie avec ma carte.
I pay with my card.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: Both spellings are correct: the y can become i before a silent e (paie) or stay (paye).

tenses.name: Imparfait
tenses.note: Watch nous payions, vous payiez: y followed by i.

tenses.name: Futur simple
tenses.note: Both spellings are correct: paierai or payerai.

tenses.name: Conditionnel présent
tenses.note: Both spellings are correct: paierais or payerais.

tenses.name: Subjonctif présent
tenses.note: Both spellings are correct. Watch the nous / vous forms: payions, payiez (y + i).

fr_pelle_noun.hook: A PELican holds the baker's long wooden PEEL in its beak, with a loaf on it: PEHL!
fr_pelle_noun.note: Une pelle is any shovel or spade. In a bakery it is the long flat paddle used to slide bread into the oven.
ex: Il sort le pain du four avec la pelle.
He takes the bread out of the oven with the peel.

fr_petrir_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe KNEADS the dough in a giant PETRI dish: pay-TREER = petri.
fr_petrir_verb.note: A regular -ir verb like finir: nous pétrissons, je pétrissais. Le pétrin is the kneading trough.
ex: Le boulanger pétrit la pâte chaque matin.
The baker kneads the dough every morning.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -ir verb, like finir: -is, -is, -it, then -iss- in the plural (nous pétrissons).

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: J'ai pétri la pâte. = I kneaded the dough.

fr_photo_noun.hook: A framed PHOTO of a big smiling TOE: foh-TOE! Feminine because it is short for la photographie.
fr_photo_noun.note: Feminine, even though it ends in -o: la photo is short for la photographie. Prendre une photo = to take a photo.
ex: Regarde cette photo de mes vacances.
Look at this photo from my vacation.

fr_pigeon_noun.hook: A PIGEON called JOHN struts round the bell tower in his red bow tie: pee-ZHOHN!
fr_pigeon_noun.note: Same word as English, but the g is soft (zh) and the end is nasal.
ex: Les pigeons mangent des miettes sur la place.
The pigeons eat crumbs in the square.

fr_planche_noun.hook: A goggled frog crouches on a PLANK, ready to PLUNGE. Plunge is an approximate cue for planche [PLAHNSH].
fr_planche_noun.note: The French final sound is sh, rather than the j sound in English plunge.
ex: Il coupe une planche de bois.
He's cutting a wooden plank.

fr_plante_noun.hook: The PLANT waters itself with a little watering can: la plante = the plant, almost the same word.
fr_plante_noun.note: A cognate: plante looks and means like plant, but the French ends in -e and is feminine.
ex: Il y a une plante sur chaque table.
There is a plant on every table.

fr_plateau_noun.hook: The baking TRAY is the flat top of a rocky PLATEAU: plah-TOH = plateau.
ex: Pose les petits pains sur le plateau.
Put the rolls on the tray.

falseFriend.note: A tray first of all. It also means a plateau (a flat-topped hill), as in English.

fr_pomme_noun.hook: The APPLE wears a woolly hat with a big POM-POM: POM = pomme.
fr_pomme_noun.note: Une pomme de terre (an “earth apple”) is a potato. Un jus de pomme = apple juice.
ex: Je prends une tarte aux pommes.
I’ll have an apple tart.

fr_porte_noun.hook: This old side door has a ship's ANCHOR on it and a round brass PORTHOLE: PORT! La porte is the door.
fr_porte_noun.note: Ouvrir la porte = to open the door; fermer la porte = to close it.
ex: La porte de la cuisine est ouverte.
The kitchen door is open.

falseFriend.note: A door, not a port. A harbor is le port.

fr_poubelle_noun.hook: The big green BIN has a BELL on its lid that rings every time you throw something in: pou-BELLE! (It is named after Monsieur Poubelle, who brought trash cans to Paris.)
fr_poubelle_noun.note: Jeter à la poubelle = to throw in the trash. Named after Monsieur Poubelle, the Paris official who brought in garbage cans in 1884.
ex: Jette ça à la poubelle.
Throw that in the trash.

fr_pourboire_noun.hook: A POOR BOAR (poor-BWAHR) in patched overalls beams as a coin drops into his cup: a TIP!
fr_pourboire_noun.note: Word by word it means "for drinking": pour + boire.
ex: Nous avons laissé un pourboire au serveur.
We left a tip for the waiter.

fr_prix_noun.hook: A gold PRIZE rosette with a PRICE tag hanging off it. Le prix means both, and PREE is the start of PRIZE.
ex: Quel est le prix de ce livre ?
What is the price of this book?

falseFriend.note: Price as well as prize. In a shop it is always the price: quel est le prix ?

fr_pyramide_noun.hook: The PYRAMID is PEERING through a little spyglass: PEER-a-meed = pyramid.
fr_pyramide_noun.note: Feminine, though it looks like the English: UNE pyramide. The y sounds like ee.
ex: La pyramide a quatre triangles et un carré.
The pyramid has four triangles and a square.

fr_regle_noun.hook: The RULER wears a crown and a red cape: it looks very REGAL! REHGL.
fr_regle_noun.note: Also a rule: les règles du jeu = the rules of the game.
ex: Trace un trait avec ta règle.
Draw a line with your ruler.

fr_rendez_vous_noun.hook: A hedgehog with a bouquet checks his watch: his RENDEZVOUS is late! English borrowed the same word.
fr_rendez_vous_noun.note: Prendre rendez-vous = to make an appointment. Same in the plural: les rendez-vous.
ex: J'ai rendez-vous chez le dentiste.
I have an appointment at the dentist's.

falseFriend.note: Mostly an appointment (doctor, town hall). It can be a date, but it is the everyday word for any arranged meeting.

fr_reparation_noun.hook: A little blue robot tightens the wheel nut to REPAIR a bicycle. Réparation [ray-pah-rah-SYOHN] means repair; this is a meaning picture, not a full sound pun.
fr_reparation_noun.note: Une réparation is a repair; faire réparer means to have something repaired.
ex: La réparation du vélo est terminée.
The bicycle repair is finished.

falseFriend.note: Usually a repair. It can also mean reparation (making amends), as in English.

fr_reparer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe REPAIRS a split chair leg with a clamp. Réparer [ray-pah-RAY] is related to English repair.
fr_reparer_verb.note: Réparer un vélo, une chaise, une machine: repair a bicycle, chair or machine.
ex: Mon père répare mon vélo.
My father is repairing my bike.

fr_repondre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe crouches by a little POND and ANSWERS the frog: ray-POHNDR = ray + pond.
fr_repondre_verb.note: A regular -re verb like vendre: je réponds, il répond (no ending), nous répondons. Répondre À quelqu'un = to answer someone.
ex: Le serveur répond à la question.
The waiter answers the question.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -re verb, like vendre: -s, -s, nothing, then -ons, -ez, -ent (il répond).

tenses.name: Passé composé
tenses.note: Il a répondu tout de suite. = He answered straight away.

fr_ressort_noun.hook: A tiny vacation RESORT rests on a coil SPRING. Resort loosely cues ressort [ruh-SOR].
ex: Le ressort du matelas est cassé.
The mattress spring is broken.

falseFriend.note: A spring (the coiled metal kind), not a resort. A vacation resort is une station.

fr_reveil_noun.hook: The ALARM CLOCK blows the morning bugle call, the REVEILLE: ray-VEHY.
fr_reveil_noun.note: Bakers start very early: le réveil sonne à 4 heures. Se réveiller = to wake up.
ex: Le réveil sonne à quatre heures.
The alarm clock goes off at four o’clock.

fr_ruban_noun.hook: A big red RIBBON is tied round a BANana: rew-BAHN = ri-BAN(ana).
ex: Je mets un ruban rouge sur le cadeau.
I’m putting a red ribbon on the present.

fr_sac_a_dos_noun.hook: A young DOE carries a SACK on her back: sack-a-DOE, a backpack!
fr_sac_a_dos_noun.note: Word for word: a bag (sac) for (à) the back (dos). At elementary school, a school bag is often un cartable.
ex: Mets ton cahier dans ton sac à dos.
Put your exercise book in your backpack.

fr_sac_noun.hook: A brown paper SACK stuffed with three baguettes. Sac sounds just like SACK.
ex: Mon sac est très lourd.
My bag is very heavy.

fr_salade_noun.hook: The SALAD bowl wears a LAD’s flat cap: sah-LAHD = sa + boy.
fr_salade_noun.note: Une salade can be a salad or a head of lettuce. Une salade de fruits = fruit salad.
ex: Je prends une salade verte.
I’ll have a green salad.

fr_sandwich_noun.hook: A seagull bites a giant SANDWICH and SAND pours out of it. French says sahn-DWEETSH.
fr_sandwich_noun.note: Same word as English, French pronunciation.
ex: Je mange un sandwich au fromage.
I'm eating a cheese sandwich.

fr_scier_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SAWS a plank held firmly in a clamp. Scier is pronounced [SYAY]; this is a clear action picture.
fr_scier_verb.note: An -er verb: the red beret. Scier keeps both i letters in nous sciions and vous sciiez.
ex: Il scie une planche.
He saws a plank.

fr_seau_noun.hook: A needle SEWS up the leaky BUCKET with red stitches: SOH = sew.
fr_seau_noun.note: Same sound as l’eau with an s: un seau d’eau = a bucket of water. Plural with -x: des seaux.
ex: Le seau est plein d’eau.
The bucket is full of water.

fr_sel_noun.hook: The SALT shaker is locked in a prison CELL: SEHL = cell.
fr_sel_noun.note: Usually no plural: du sel = some salt. Bread needs flour, water, salt and yeast.
ex: Ajoute une pincée de sel.
Add a pinch of salt.

fr_serveur_noun.hook: The WAITER SWERVES (sehr-VUHR) between the tables, a plate of croissants held high in each hand.
ex: Le serveur apporte l'addition.
The waiter brings the bill.

fr_serviette_noun.hook: A napkin folded into a swan sits by a little bell, waiting: "SERVE YET?" (sehr-VYEHT). British English even says serviette for a napkin.
fr_serviette_noun.note: Also a bath or beach towel.
ex: Le serveur pose une serviette sur la table.
The waiter puts a napkin on the table.

fr_signer_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SIGNS the form with a big feather pen and punches the air: SIGN... YAY! see-NYAY.
fr_signer_verb.note: Your signature is la signature. Signez ici = sign here.
ex: Signez ici, s'il vous plaît.
Sign here, please.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: A regular -er verb. The gn sounds like the ny in canyon: je signe (SEENY).

tenses.name: Impératif
tenses.note: Signez ici ! = Sign here! (no s for tu: signe !)

fr_silence_noun.hook: A kitten in woolly socks tiptoes past with a paw to its lips: SILENCE! Same word as in English, said see-LAHNS.
fr_silence_noun.note: Watch the gender: most -ence words are feminine (la patience), but le silence is masculine.
ex: Silence, s'il vous plaît !
Silence, please!

fr_soleil_noun.hook: The SUN lounges in a deckchair, SO LAZY: soh-LEHY = so la(zy).
fr_soleil_noun.note: Au soleil = in the sun. Il y a du soleil = it is sunny.
ex: On s’assoit au soleil ?
Should we sit in the sun?

fr_somme_noun_f.hook: The slate shows a SUM: 2 + 3 = 5. SOM = sum.
fr_somme_noun_f.note: Careful: LA somme is a sum, but LE somme is a short nap (faire un somme). Faire la somme = to add up.
ex: La somme de deux et trois, c'est cinq.
The sum of two and three is five.

fr_souris_noun.hook: A little MOUSE in an apron has nibbled the cheese and says SORRY: soo-REE!
fr_souris_noun.note: Same in the plural: des souris. It is also a computer mouse.
ex: Le chat chasse la souris.
The cat chases the mouse.

fr_stylo_noun.hook: A STYLISH PEN in sunglasses and a pink scarf strikes a pose: STY-LO!
fr_stylo_noun.note: Un stylo is any pen; un stylo-plume is a fountain pen, un stylo à bille a ballpoint.
ex: Tu peux me prêter un stylo ?
Can you lend me a pen?

fr_sucre_noun.hook: A giant swirly SUCKER (a lollipop) stands up in a bowl of SUGAR cubes. Sucker sounds like sucre.
ex: Tu prends du sucre dans ton café ?
Do you take sugar in your coffee?

fr_table_noun.hook: A TABBY cat dances on the café TABLE: TABBY-L, TAHBL!
fr_table_noun.note: Same spelling as English; French says TAHBL, with a short ah.
ex: Le repas est sur la table.
The meal is on the table.

fr_tableau_affichage_noun.hook: A little orange FISH pins the alphabet onto the board: d'a-FISH-age! Tap it to hear every letter.
fr_tableau_affichage_noun.note: Afficher = to put up (a poster or notice). Tableau is masculine, so the whole thing is le tableau d'affichage.
ex: Les lettres sont sur le tableau d'affichage.
The letters are on the notice board.

fr_tableau_noun.hook: The green BOARD stands on its own wooden TABLE: TABLE, OH! tah-BLOH.
fr_tableau_noun.note: Au tableau ! = to the board! Words in -eau take -x in the plural: les tableaux.
ex: Écris ton nom au tableau.
Write your name on the board.

falseFriend.note: The classroom board, or a painting. Not a tableau (a staged scene) in everyday French.

fr_tablier_noun.hook: A little TABLE wears an APRON and kicks up a leg: "TABLE, YAY!" = tah-blee-YAY.
fr_tablier_noun.note: Mettre son tablier = to put on your apron.
ex: Le boulanger met son tablier blanc.
The baker puts on his white apron.

fr_tapis_noun.hook: A TAPIR (tah-PEE) sits proudly in the middle of its RUG, as if it owned it.
fr_tapis_noun.note: Same in the plural: des tapis.
ex: Le chat dort sur le tapis.
The cat sleeps on the rug.

falseFriend.note: A rug or carpet, not a tapestry. A tapestry is une tapisserie.

fr_tarte_noun.hook: A bright fruit TART with strawberries, blueberries and apricots. Tarte is just TART with a French accent.
ex: Ma mère fait une tarte aux pommes.
My mother is making an apple tart.

fr_tasse_noun.hook: Someone TOSSES (TAHS) the CUP right off its saucer, tea and all!
fr_tasse_noun.note: Une tasse de thé = a cup of tea.
ex: Je voudrais une tasse de thé.
I'd like a cup of tea.

fr_telephone_noun.hook: The red TELEPHONE rings and bounces, having FUN: tay-lay-FON = tele + fun.
fr_telephone_noun.note: Masculine: LE téléphone. Au téléphone = on the phone. Téléphoner à quelqu’un = to phone someone.
ex: Le téléphone sonne au guichet.
The phone is ringing at the counter.

fr_the_noun.hook: A ginger cat sits on the counter, its long fluffy TAIL (TAY) by a cup of TEA.
fr_the_noun.note: The h is silent: thé sounds just like TAY.
ex: Ma grand-mère boit du thé à cinq heures.
My grandmother drinks tea at five o'clock.

fr_timbre_noun.hook: The STAMP shows a big red TAMBOURINE: TAM-bourine... TANBR!
ex: Il faut un timbre pour envoyer la lettre.
You need a stamp to send the letter.

falseFriend.note: A postage stamp. It also means timbre (the tone of a voice or a bell), as in English.

fr_tranche_noun.hook: A SLICE of bread in a TRENCH coat: TRAHNSH = trench.
fr_tranche_noun.note: Une tranche de pain = a slice of bread. Le pain de mie en tranches = sliced bread.
ex: Tu veux une tranche de pain ?
Do you want a slice of bread?

fr_triangle_noun.hook: Ting! The musical TRIANGLE is a triangle too, the same word said the French way: tree-YAHNGL.
fr_triangle_noun.note: Not in the course word list. Same word for the shape and the musical instrument.
ex: Le triangle a trois côtés.
The triangle has three sides.

fr_tronc_noun.en: donation box (in a church); also: tree trunk
fr_tronc_noun.hook: A baby elephant uses its TRUNK to drop a coin into the church's TRONC, the donation box. Trunk sounds like tronc (TROHN).
fr_tronc_noun.note: The c is silent and the on is nasal. Le tronc is also the trunk of a tree.
ex: L'arbre a un tronc énorme.
The tree has an enormous trunk.

fr_trou_noun.hook: A tiny TROOP of wind-up toy soldiers marches into a HOLE. TROOP without its final p sounds like trou [TROO].
fr_trou_noun.note: French trou ends in the vowel oo; the final p of English troop is omitted.
ex: Il y a un trou dans le sol.
There is a hole in the floor.

fr_trousse_noun.hook: The PENCIL CASE waves a little white TRUCE flag: no more pencil fights! TROOSS = truce.
fr_trousse_noun.note: Une trousse is any small zipped kit: une trousse de toilette is a wash bag.
ex: J'ai oublié ma trousse !
I forgot my pencil case!

fr_valise_noun.hook: The SUITCASE trots along on a red dog LEASH: vah-LEEZ = (a) leash.
fr_valise_noun.note: Faire sa valise = to pack your suitcase.
ex: Ma valise est trop lourde !
My suitcase is too heavy!

fr_velo_noun.hook: The red BIKE zooms off at top VELOCITY, leaving a puff of dust: vay-LOH = velo(city).
fr_velo_noun.note: À vélo = by bike. Faire du vélo = to ride a bike.
ex: Elle arrive au café à vélo.
She comes to the café by bike.

fr_vendre_verb.hook: Monsieur Verbe SELLS a fresh baguette across the counter. Think of English VEND (to sell, as in a vending machine): vend, vendre.
ex: Il vend des fruits au marché.
He sells fruit at the market.

tenses.name: Présent
tenses.note: il vend has no ending: the d is silent.

fr_vent_noun.hook: A little blue VAN puffs out a big gust of WIND: VAHN = van.
fr_vent_noun.note: The t is silent. Il y a du vent = it is windy.
ex: Il y a du vent sur la terrasse.
It’s windy on the terrace.

falseFriend.note: Wind, not a vent. An air vent is une grille d'aération.

fr_verre_noun.hook: The glass of water shades its eyes and looks around: "WHERE?" (VEHR). Where sounds like verre.
fr_verre_noun.note: Le verre = the glass; l'eau (feminine!) = water. The whole phrase takes le from verre.
ex: Tu veux un verre de jus ?
Do you want a glass of juice?

fr_verrou_noun.hook: A tiny kangaroo grips a sliding door BOLT. Roo cues the ending of verrou [veh-ROO]; the first syllable is veh.
fr_verrou_noun.note: A verrou is a sliding bolt, not a key-operated lock (une serrure).
ex: Il ferme la porte au verrou.
He bolts the door.

fr_vis_noun.hook: Two toy GEESE hold a SCREW. Vis [VEES] rhymes with geese; the first consonant is v.
ex: Il serre la vis avec un tournevis.
He tightens the screw with a screwdriver.
fr_vis_noun.note: Pronounce VEES, rhyming with geese. The singular and plural are spelled vis.

falseFriend.note: A screw, not a vice (vise). A vice for gripping work is un étau.
